batch.title: Agroforestry T4 — five holds reviewed and corrected
batch.notes: All five corrected records approved by Pete in chat ("I approved all"). Approvals logged on branch. Open methodology decisions: Sahel FMNR scope and Haile family applicability. Approval accepts corrected encoding, not a global threshold.

units.citation: Sprenkle-Hyppolite, S., Griscom, B., Griffey, V., Munshi, E., & Chapman, M. (2024). Maximizing tree carbon in croplands and grazing lands while sustaining yields. Carbon Balance and Management, 19(1), 23.
units.quote:
While definitions of forests using tree cover differ 
(depending on the use and ecosystem, definitions range 
from 10 to 30%) and agriculture does occur in areas with 
> 25% tree cover, we used 25% tree cover as a cutoff in 
order to avoid any double counting of natural climate 
solution potential with forestry-based solutions (please 
see the following paragraph for further discussion of tree 
cover). This cutoff also avoids the need for distinguish­
ing high-shade agroforestry from natural forests using 
remote sensing, which is not yet available globally [30].

relationship.note: Avoids double counting agricultural and forestry natural climate solutions; source explicitly acknowledges agriculture above 25% tree cover. Not a biological suitability threshold.

units.question: Correction applied on branch; approved by Pete in chat. Sprenkle-Hyppolite PDF p4 Geospatial data processing: 25% separates agricultural and forestry NCS accounting and avoids distinguishing high-shade agroforestry from natural forests. Source explicitly allows agriculture above 25%. Removed executable threshold. Require evidence of trees within agricultural land before spatial aggregation; coarse forest/crop mixture is insufficient.
units.crop_note: Complete source page; corrected quote shown alongside. Click image to enlarge.

plain.practice: Practice: agroforestry → planted silvoarable (Alley cropping; Tree intercropping; Planted boundary / live fence on cropland).
plain.described: Your original hold: need to be carefull as if pixel size large then forest and cropland will get muddled togher suggesting that there are trees in croplands (where as they may be spatially disaggregrated and there are no trees in croplands) -> would need a decent dataset on trees in cropland or rangeland to make this work.
plain.claim: Sprenkle-Hyppolite PDF p4 Geospatial data processing: 25% separates agricultural and forestry NCS accounting and avoids distinguishing high-shade agroforestry from natural forests. Source explicitly allows agriculture above 25%. Removed executable threshold. Require evidence of trees within agricultural land before spatial aggregation; coarse forest/crop mixture is insufficient.
plain.role: Retained evidence; no approved threshold contribution.

units.citation: Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration Promotes Expansion of Trees on Croplands in the Sahel (2025). Research Square preprint.
units.quote:
Yet, the scattered distribution of trees on croplands has historically made it difficult to track 
118 
changes over time using coarse-resolution satellite imagery34. To overcome this limitation, we 
119 
reconstructed annual tree cover from 1999 to 2024 across the Sahel (300–800 mm mean 
120 
annual rainfall) using dry-season median composites from Landsat 7, 8, and 9. We focused 
121 
specifically on 2.4 million km² of croplands identified in the 2000 land cover map38, and applied 
122 
a deep learning model trained on the 9.9 billion tree detections29 to predict annual percentage 
123 
tree cover at 15 m resolution (Fig. 1a). The resulting maps reveal large areas with high tree 
124 
cover on croplands, particularly in Senegal, Niger, and northern Nigeria (Fig. 1b–c). 
125

relationship.note: Sahel reconstruction study domain, not FMNR establishment limits.

units.question: Correction applied on branch; approved by Pete in chat. PDF p5 Results defines a Sahel cropland reconstruction domain (300-800 mm), not physiological limits. Removed hard bounds; retained study domain. Proposed semi-arid Sahel FMNR scope is a separate pending methodology decision.

Your original hold: it is the study area you are correct, but:
